title: How Snowmen (And Snowwomen) Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the history and culture of snowmen and snow people, from prehistoric art and a 1380s-era Book of Hours illumination through Michelangelo's commissioned snowman, the 1511 Miracle of Brussels snow festival, the 1665 Fort Schenectady snowmen guards, Mary Dillwyn's early photograph, and the Victorian shaping of the modern snowman. They cover Snegurochka and Ded Moroz, the Nazi-era cartoon Der Schneemann, Frosty the Snowman (song and Rankin/Bass specials), Raymond Briggs' The Snowman with David Bowie's intro, snowman pop culture (Calvin and Hobbs, Olaf, Jack Frost), Zurich's Sechseläuten snowman burning, Gaylord Michigan's Alpinfest, snowman world records in Bethel, Maine and Japan's yuki daruma, tips for building snowmen, and naming ideas. The episode closes with a sponsor-style call-out for Cooperative for Education (CoEd) in Guatemala and a listener mail segment.

segments.title: Opening banter and snowman origins
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with off-topic sauna and Bluetooth banter, then introduce the episode on snow people and early snowman art, including Bob Eckstein's research and the Book of Hours snowman depiction.

segments.title: Michelangelo, Brussels and early snowman history
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Michelangelo's commissioned giant snowman in Florence, the 1511 Miracle of Brussels snow festival named after poet Jan Smeken, and the 1690 Fort Schenectady attack where snowmen were reportedly used as guards.

segments.title: Early photographs and the Victorian snowman
segments.summary: Mary Dillwyn's early photograph of her parents making a snowman is described, and the hosts argue the modern snowman image took shape in the Victorian era alongside Christmas traditions.

segments.title: Snegurochka and Ded Moroz
segments.summary: The Russian snow maiden Snegurochka is told as a folk tale in which she melts after a fire-jumping game; she was later revived as the granddaughter of Ded Moroz, Russia's Grandpa Frost, who gives presents around New Year.

segments.title: Der Schneemann Nazi-era cartoon
segments.summary: The hosts describe the 1944 German short Der Schneemann, commissioned under Joseph Goebbels and made by Hans Fischer-Kusten, and note his son's claim that it contains no political propaganda.

segments.title: Frosty the Snowman song and specials
segments.summary: The origin of the Frosty the Snowman song by Steve Nelson and Jack Rollins, written for Gene Autry, its Armonk, New York setting, and the Rankin/Bass TV specials and sequels.

segments.title: The Snowman by Raymond Briggs and David Bowie
segments.summary: The wordless picture book and Channel 4 TV adaptation The Snowman by Raymond Briggs, and the story of David Bowie recording the intro that replaced Briggs's for American audiences.

segments.title: Snowmen in pop culture
segments.summary: Calvin's snowmen in Calvin and Hobbs, Olaf in Frozen, and the 1998 movie Jack Frost starring Michael Keaton, which Roger Ebert disliked.

segments.title: Burning snowmen to welcome spring
segments.summary: Zurich's Sechseläuten festival burns a snowman stuffed with dynamite to mark the end of winter, and Gaylord Michigan's Alpinfest burns a snowman filled with written worries.

segments.title: Snowman world records and building tips
segments.summary: Records include the tall snowmen in Bethel, Maine and the most snowmen in Japan's Sapporo in 2003, plus the yuki daruma two-ball style. The hosts give tips on packing snow and rolling balls, and decorating with Martha Stewart's pine cone pipe idea.

segments.title: Snowman naming suggestions
segments.summary: The hosts recommend naming snowmen and share name suggestions from KidsAbout.

segments.title: CoEd sponsorship call-out
segments.summary: Hosts promote Cooperative for Education in Guatemala and its thousand girls sponsorship initiative.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: Closing remarks, the CoEd sponsorship details and contact information for the show.
